chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Maḥmūd, who said:

I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: A man becomes junub, and khaluq, perfume, and some adhesive substance such as Roman gum and ṭarār and the like affect his body and head. Then he performs ghusl, and when he has finished, he finds something on his body that has remained from the trace of the khaluq, perfume, and other than that. So he said: “There is no harm.”

key_terms.الْخَلُوقُ: a scented cosmetic or perfume substance applied to the body
key_terms.عِلْكِ الرُّومِ: Roman gum, a sticky adhesive substance
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; no legal problem
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: enters the state of janabah requiring ghusl

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl after janabah valid if traces of perfume or sticky substances remain on the body?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ghusl after janabah when traces of perfume or adhesive substances remain on the body. Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام states that there is no problem if such residual traces are found after completing the ghusl.
